proposedTestOnlyRule.type: Branch-local mechanic for one synthetic W2 fixture; not canonical.

definitions.restrainedSystemMassLb: Restrained body + attached/worn gear and cargo + Conjure Rope, each counted once.
definitions.upwardRestraintLoadLb: Equal to restrainedSystemMassLb. This is a new 1:1 test convention in pound-equivalent units, not a source-defined physical-force conversion.
definitions.effectiveCapacityLb: Lower of the bound Conjure Rope operational playtest limit of 300 lb and the newly defined 250-lb TEST_ONLY complete assembly rating. These values are limited to this reviewed branch; this proposal makes no canon-promotion claim.
definitions.tautBehavior: Inextensible for this test. Slack is consumed geometrically; at first taut contact, vertical velocity is set to zero before immediate quasi-static sampling, so no impact or dynamic multiplier is introduced.
definitions.threshold: At each taut sample and every subsequent applicable mass change, test both limits independently. Each component fails only if its current load exceeds its rating; equality holds. If both limits are exceeded, both failure results apply.
definitions.eventEnd: This W2 branch treats upward displacement as a bounded TEST_ONLY event from t=18 through t=24 at 10 ft/s. The event is the only upward support and terminates at t=24. If the tether releases during the event, only still-scheduled displacement before t=24 applies. Ordinary Falling begins at t=24 if unsupported.
definitions.loadRecheck: Never grandfather the first-taut sample. Recalculate the full current body + attached/worn gear/cargo + rope load whenever an applicable mass change occurs while connected; apply rope overload and assembly release immediately.
definitions.failureAssembly: For the branch-only 250-lb assembly, the support-side synthetic weak link releases above 250 lb without damaging/moving the fixed support. The rope itself remains unless its separate 300-lb limit is exceeded.

sequence: Use only the supplied synthetic 60-ft upward movement schedule, beginning at t=18 and ending at t=24; do not assert an actual spell cast, actor, campaign event, or additional Reverse Gravity source rule.
The event requests 10 ft/s upward movement. Consume only the measured 40.4 ft tether slack as the target rises; no Rope command lifts, hauls, or draws slack for free.

At first taut contact (t=22.04 in the aligned base fixture, after exactly 40.4 ft of +z travel), stop vertical velocity before immediate quasi-static sampling. A load within both ratings holds the target there and blocks only the remaining movement scheduled before t=24.

If the assembly load exceeds 250 lb, release its support-side synthetic weak link immediately. If the rope load exceeds 300 lb, the whole rope immediately vanishes under its bound overload rule. Evaluate these results independently; simultaneous exceedance causes both.
Recheck both current limits immediately after every applicable mass change, including changes after the first-taut sample.
If a restraint ends before t=24, apply only the remaining 10-ft/s scheduled displacement until t=24; never replay prior movement.

At t=24 the synthetic upward event ends. The tether anchored below does not keep the target aloft; ordinary Falling starts, with its rescue window, Fall Marker, landing, damage, and condition handled by the bound provisional falling procedure for this TEST_ONLY review.
Keep body, gear, cargo, rope, support, assembly, and custody records; preserve Conjure Rope's original t=600-second expiry.

cast.creationPointPremise: Before t=0 casting, the full 0.8-by-0.8-by-1.45-ft TEST_ONLY creation cell centered at [-2.2,0,2.225] (bounds x[-2.6,-1.8], y[-0.4,0.4], z[1.5,2.95]) is clear of creatures, gear and objects. It begins exactly at the shelf top z=1.5 and has no positive-volume overlap with the shelf. The complete 50-ft, 0.05-ft-diameter rope materializes as one continuous, unbroken TEST_ONLY coil wholly inside the cell, with measured envelope 0.70-by-0.70-by-1.35 ft (0.6615 ft3), bounding the 0.098175 ft3 rope material. The continuous centerline length is explicitly stipulated and measured at exactly 50.000 ft while packed in that envelope. No analytic turn recipe or uncounted inter-level connectors are asserted; the measured coil is a branch premise, not a general creation rule. The coil rests on the shelf.

attachmentSetup.operation: From t=0 to t=6, TEST_HANDLER_B stands at [0,1,0] on the upper platform. TEST_HANDLER_A walks from [-1,2,0] to pickup stance [-1,0,0] (nearest coil-envelope point 1.724 ft away) and lifts/supports the 10-lb coil. A draws out its free end by hand and presents it at handoff point [-0.5,0,0.9]. That point is 1.030 ft from A's pickup stance and 1.436 ft from B; the target D-ring [0,0,1.5] is 1.803 ft from B and 0.781 ft from the handoff point. B receives the end from A and clips it to the consenting target's side D-ring within B's 2.25-ft reach. A supports the coil throughout; B does not retrieve the end directly from the shelf. These are supported manual operations; no Rope command.

From t=6 to t=14, after B clips the upper end, A carries the coil along the supported upper platform to stair entrance [-1,2,0], descends TEST_SERVICE_STAIR_01, and manually pays out the continuous rope along the clear D-ring-to-patch segment from [0,0,1.5] to [0.6,0,-8.5] (10.017984 ft). A lays 39.260906 ft as loose irregular bights within TEST_LOWER_SLACK_PATCH_01, returning the running line to that patch entry, then routes the final 0.721110-ft lead from [0.6,0,-8.5] to bracket [0,0,-8.1] and secures the rope end. Total deployed length is exactly 50.000000 ft; relative to the 9.6-ft direct taut endpoint distance, slack is 1.139094 ft of leader detour plus 39.260906 ft of bights = 40.400000 ft. No tray, reel, passive guide, powered haul, flight, levitation, Rope command, or free slack-drawing lift.

Handler A exits to the lower supported bay [-1,2,-8.5], Handler B exits to the upper bay [-2,2,0], and the caster remains at [3,-2,0]. They are clear of the target/cargo swept volume and rope channel. Inspect surfaces, attachments, rope slack, permissions and clearances before the upward event starts at t=18.

support.kind: Synthetic fixed wall bracket on the lower service-channel wall, 0.4 ft above the supported lower ledge.
support.ratingScope: TEST_ONLY complete load-bearing assembly rating. Bracket, support-side weak link, both terminal connections, both connectors, waist harness and D-ring are included within the same 250-lb rating; no included element receives a higher independent capacity.
support.overrating: Above 250 lb, the support-side weak link releases immediately; the fixed bracket and support-side connector remain with the fixture. The intact rope stays attached to the target-side harness connector unless its separate 300-lb overload condition is also met.

tether.path: One continuous unbroken rope. At t=18 its deployed path runs from target D-ring [0,0,1.5] along a straight, unobstructed diagonal leader to patch entry [0.6,0,-8.5] (10.017984 ft), through 39.260906 ft of loose bights within TEST_LOWER_SLACK_PATCH_01 returning to that patch entry, then along a straight unobstructed 0.721110-ft return lead to fixed bracket [0,0,-8.1]. These portions total 50.000000 ft. The direct taut endpoint distance from D-ring to bracket is 9.6 ft. The two leaders exceed that direct distance by 1.139094 ft; together with the 39.260906-ft bights this is the full 40.400000-ft slack. The leaders can slide and straighten through the specified open clearance corridor; no pulley, guide, bend contact, or load-bearing routing device is present. Under tension the line straightens to the direct D-ring-to-bracket span.
tether.slackStorage: At t=18, direct D-ring-to-bracket endpoint distance is 9.6 ft and rope length is 50 ft. The continuous deployed path is D-ring [0,0,1.5] to patch entry [0.6,0,-8.5] (10.017984 ft), through 39.260906 ft of loose irregular bights on the patch and returning to that entry, then patch entry to bracket [0,0,-8.1] (0.721110 ft). These line portions total 50.000000 ft. The routed leaders add 1.139094 ft beyond the 9.6-ft direct endpoint distance; together with the 39.260906-ft bights they account for the full 40.400000-ft slack. The patch is an open ledge, not a tray or reel. The leaders can slide and straighten through the defined corridor as the target rises; there is no powered or commanded hauling.
tether.slackTakeup: The taut reference is the direct distance from the D-ring to the fixed bracket, 9.6 ft. At t=18 the continuous route has 1.139094 ft of leader detour plus 39.260906 ft of loose bights, totaling 40.400000 ft beyond that reference. In the unobstructed TEST_ONLY corridor, increasing endpoint separation by 1 ft per 1 ft of target +z travel consumes this total; first taut remains at 40.4 ft of rise, t=22.04.
tether.endpointAccess: For the upper handoff, A presents the free end at [-0.5,0,0.9] to B at [0,1,0] (1.436 ft); B clips it to the target D-ring [0,0,1.5] (1.803 ft from B), both within 2.25-ft reach. A approaches the lower bracket from [-1,1,-8.5], 1.47 ft from [0,0,-8.1], within reach. The deployed route has a 10.017984-ft leader from D-ring to patch entry [0.6,0,-8.5], 39.260906 ft of loose bights on the patch, and a 0.721110-ft return lead to the bracket; all portions are counted once.
